all_26_live_guards.legal_basis: East Whiteland Township municipal curative amendment under the PA Municipalities Planning Code, developed with a resident working group beginning May 2026; a Sept. 24, 2026 public hearing was set to consider adoption of the resulting ordinance
all_26_live_guards.trigger: Regulatory gap combined with a specific, highly contested project: developer Green Fig's proposal (later expanded to 1.7 million sq ft) for a data center on Swedesford Road, which drew sustained community opposition; the township already had an earlier, separately approved 2024 data-center plan on the same site.
all_26_live_guards.current_status: Nearing resolution as of 2026-09-23. The 180-day curative-amendment clock started in March 2026 (per The Center Square); Green Fig withdrew its expanded 1.7-million-sq-ft application in May 2026 amid sustained opposition and signaled intent to instead pursue its earlier, previously approved 2024 plan. A resident working group helped draft the resulting 'Data Center Ordinance,' for which the Board of Supervisors set a Sept. 24, 2026 public hearing to consider adoption (one day after this research pass); the pending Sentinel/Green Fig application is not on that hearing's agenda.
all_26_live_guards.affected_projects: Green Fig/Sentinel data center proposal on Swedesford Road; the expanded 1.7-million-sq-ft version was withdrawn in May 2026, with the developer expected to instead pursue its earlier-approved 2024 plan (details of that plan not confirmed in this pass).
all_26_live_guards.outcome: East Whiteland Township Board of Supervisors initiated a municipal curative amendment in March 2026 to add data-center zoning standards; a resident working group helped draft the resulting ordinance, which was scheduled for a Sept. 24, 2026 adoption hearing.
